candidates.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
candidates.content: Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents. TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue. An event-driven finite-state machine (FSM) uses completed actions and delivered information to update task states and evaluate outcomes. TARSphere-Harness, its embodied brain harness, lets a frozen multimodal large language model (MLLM) act through multi-level executable skills, using observations, hierarchical memory, and execution feedback to revise its decisions. On this foundation, agent-in-the-loop curation aligns task semantics, causal dependencies, and scene geometry to construct TARSphere-Bench: 360 episodes across 30 indoor scenes. candidates.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
candidates.content: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) relies on evaluation feedback to assess progress and guide further research, yet repeatedly running complex benchmarks is costly and slows iteration. Human experts reduce this cost by selecting benchmark subsets or designing compact suites. We ask whether AI agents can automate this design process and introduce EvalResearchBench (ERB), a benchmark for autonomous evaluation research. Given target materials, development references, candidate APIs, and fixed time and API budgets, an agent called the researcher selects or synthesizes tasks, implements graders, and revises them in pilot tests before freezing an executable evaluator for coding, co-work, and reasoning. We study 9 researchers and 13 candidate models and compare each frozen evaluator with 14 target benchmarks on score concordance and pairwise agreement. The best evaluators order about 75\% of candidate pairs as the targets do, below the 91\% ceiling set by disagreements among the targets. No researcher leads on every metric, and the best evaluator on development targets is not the best on sealed targets hidden from the researcher. A human-designed sample of public tasks remains a strong base

candidates.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
candidates.content: Diffusion language models can write several tokens in one forward pass, and they decide during generation how many passes to spend. Two outputs of the same token length can therefore vary a lot in cost. To understand the underlying factors of this cost variation, we analyze two diffusion models across 10 tasks. We find that the number of forward passes per token depends heavily on the task. Text copied or lightly edited from the input is cheap, while open-ended writing is costly. In DiffusionGemma, generating a token for story writing requires more than three times as many forward passes as for grammar correction. Two output properties explain much of this gap: how much of it is new relative to the input, and how rare its words are within the task. The same holds within a single response when thinking is involved. The final answer is cheap when it repeats the model's reasoning trace and costly when it adds something new. In multilingual generation, we find that highly tokenized languages also require more passes per token, adding to the cost they already pay with more tokens. candidates.title: CPSF6 maintains genomic stability by stabilizing RAD52 and promoting CHK1 activation
candidates.content: Abstract RAD52 and CHK1 are critical factors that play pleiotropic roles in the DNA damage response (DDR), including the resolution of transcription–replication conflicts (TRCs). However, how their functions are modulated remains incomplete. Here, we reveal that the cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor subunit 6 (CPSF6) is an unexpected DDR factor that enhances RAD52 stability and CHK1 activation. Specifically, CPSF6 competitively interacts with RAD52, thereby preventing RAD52 from interacting with the E3 ubiquitin ligase UHRF1 and subsequent proteasomal degradation. In addition, CPSF6 enhances the ATR–CHK1 interaction to promote CHK1 activation, thereby facilitating the activation of downstream CHK1–PLK1–RAD51 pathway. The dual functions of CPSF6 in RAD52 stabilization and CHK1 activation contribute to its role in TRC resolution. CPSF6 depletion causes R-loop accumulation and transcription-associated DNA damage. Notably, these roles of CPSF6 in the DDR are independent of its canonical role in pre-mRNA 3′-end processing. candidates.title: NEAT1 remodeling rewires the MYC degradation pathway
candidates.content: Abstract MYC is among the most frequently amplified oncogenes in human cancer, yet its intrinsically disordered nature has rendered it refractory to direct pharmacological targeting. Here, we demonstrate that the long noncoding RNA NEAT1_1 functions as a molecular gatekeeper that controls MYC protein stability by regulating its access to the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR5. We show that NEAT1_1 forms a ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex with both MYC and UBR5, and that NEAT1_1 suppression disrupts this interaction, leading to decreased MYC polyubiquitination and enhanced protein stability. To systematically map the regulatory architecture of NEAT1_1 without altering its abundance, we screened 88 antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) mixmers tiling across the transcript. Strikingly, this phenotypic screen identified region-specific mixmers that elicit bidirectional control over MYC, either driving robust MYC destabilization or promoting its stabilization in a strictly expression-independent manner. Mechanistically, MYC-destabilizing mixmers selectively enhance the interaction between MYC and UBR5 to accelerate proteasomal degradation. candidates.title: Emerging roles of RIF1 in mitosis
candidates.content: Abstract Faithful chromosome segregation during cell division requires precise coordination of kinase– and phosphatase–driven signaling pathways. Defects in this balance can cause chromosome missegregation and cytokinesis failure, resulting in genomic instability. Rap1-interacting factor 1 (RIF1) is known for its interphase functions in DNA damage repair, DNA replication timing, and chromatin organization. However, recent work has established RIF1 as a critical mitotic regulator that functions primarily through its role as a protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) adaptor. During early mitosis, the localization of RIF1 to the mitotic apparatus is thought to be actively suppressed by mitotic kinases, including cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1), aurora kinase B (AURKB), and polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1), preventing premature PP1 engagement and dephosphorylation. Following anaphase onset, relief of this inhibition allows PLK1-interacting checkpoint helicase (PICH)–dependent recruitment of RIF1 to ultrafine anaphase DNA bridges (UFBs), where RIF1-associated PP1 activity determines pathway choice for UFB resolution. candidates.title: Metabolic engineering of Yarrowia lipolytica for higher fatty alcohol production
candidates.content: Fatty alcohols are versatile chemicals with growing demand across a broad range of industries, yet conventional production methods pose environmental challenges. Microbial biosynthesis offers a promising alternative, if hosts can be engineered to achieve high product titers. The industrially relevant oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica is well suited to this challenge because of its natural capacity for lipid metabolism. Here, we engineered Y. lipolytica W29 for fatty alcohol production by disrupting pathways involved in lipogenesis and fatty alcohol oxidation, identifying fatty alcohol oxidation as a major constraint on product accumulation. Initial engineering yielded fatty alcohol titers of 2.5 g/L from 40 g/L glucose. Subsequent optimization of media supplements and nutrient concentrations, combined with deletion of the citrate transporter CEX1 and addition of 1% Tergitol to the extractive culture medium, increased titers to 10.9 g/L in shake flasks with 80 g/L glucose and a carbon-to-nitrogen ratio of 60. candidates.title: Dysregulated mechanoregulation of load-induced bone adaptation in prematurely aged mice: insights from a micro-multiphysics agent-based model
candidates.content: Bone exhibits remarkable ability to adapt to varying mechanical demands. Aging can lead to changes in distribution of cells and proteins that directly affect bone formation and resorption. Given the inherent challenges of quantifying these cellular and protein alterations in vivo, innovative in silico tools have proven useful to contribute to studying the impact of aging on bone mechanobiology and associated cellular mechanisms. Here, we employed an agent-based in silico analysis of in vivo micro-computed tomography data of prematurely aged mice to examine the effects of aging and mechanical loading on bone cells and their mechanome, the intrinsic cellular system sensing mechanical forces. Our results from applying a micro-multiphysics agent-based model to an in vivo model of premature aging (PolG) showed that aging disrupts mechanoregulation of load-induced bone formation and resorption by eliminating the increase in bone formation through diminished osteoblast activity and mineralization, alongside mechanomic alterations. candidates.title: Integrating Genetic Domestication and Model-Guided Kill-Switch Engineering in a Non-Model Bacterial Therapeutic
candidates.content: Engineered bacteria offer programmable cancer immunotherapies, but engineering tractability does not always align with therapeutic suitability. The attenuated intracellular vaccine strain Brucella melitensis {Delta}vjbR (Bm{Delta}vjbR) shows promise as an immunotherapy chassis, yet its translation requires reliable control and containment systems that remain difficult to engineer with the limited genetic tools available. Here, we establish a genetic domestication workflow that connects genetic part generation and quantitative evaluation with model-guided circuit design. Through mutagenesis and screening, we generated and characterized genetic part libraries, including promoters spanning two orders of magnitude in activity, a panel of ribosome-binding sites, and highly functional terminators. We also evaluated fluorescent reporters, plasmid compatibility, and three inducible regulatory systems. These host-specific measurements informed mathematical modeling to guide the selection of a doxycycline-inducible Cas9/gRNA kill-switch architecture before construction. candidates.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.31314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). Extended evaluations at depths up to 50 turns confirm that the dissociation persists beyond the core benchmark, while Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 points on immutable constraints. candidates.title: CrisiLangs: A Multilingual Resource for Crisis Warning Generation
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.31356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Communicating with the public during an emergency entails issuing warning messages promptly. In Europe, it often requires producing them in more than one language. Recent work has shown that language models can be trained to generate warning messages as a crisis unfolds, but the available data covers only English. To fill this gap, we present CrisiLangs, a multilingual extension of CrisiText (an English dataset of crisis events paired with warning messages written according to expert communication guidelines) to Italian, Bulgarian, German, and Greek. Expert native speakers translated the warning messages of 1,000 events drawn from 411 scenarios, for a total of 5,000 event-message pairs across five languages. We test the resource to fine-tune a multilingual model on all five languages jointly, with and without the emergency guidelines in the prompt, and compare it with a zero-shot baseline. The fine-tuned models outperform the baseline on ROUGE-L, BLEU and BERTScore in every language and configuration. candidates.content: arXiv:2610.30277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While artificial intelligence has made rapid progress in mathematical reasoning, many open problems depend on structure that is revealed only through large-scale computational exploration and analytical synthesis. One such example is Lehmer's problem from 1933. It asks whether the Mahler measure of an integer polynomial, which measures how far its roots stray from the unit circle, can be made arbitrarily small. Previously, constructing irreducible polynomials with integer coefficients and small Mahler measure has been carried out systematically only for even degrees $d \le 180$. At higher degrees, Boyd's analytical one-parameter family frequently factors, skipping nearly 50% of target degrees and leaving no general construction for arbitrary $d$. Here, we address the high-degree regime through a human-AI discovery loop, in which we extend the conversational prompting with a fast numerical pipeline, an exact symbolic verifier, and large-scale distributed search. candidates.title: RIPPLE: Recovery Internalization through Process-Level Policy Learning and Effect-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Agentic Coding
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.31276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon coding agents can observe a failure and generate a plausible critique yet continue along the same incorrect trajectory. We call this the Critique-to-Action Handoff Gap. We introduce RIPPLE, a recovery-oriented training framework that internalizes process-level guidance into a single self-recovering policy. A prefix-only teacher provides evidence-grounded recovery supervision without access to future actions or terminal outcomes. After lightweight distillation, reinforcement learning assigns stage-specific credit to reflection triggering, diagnosis, and corrective action. Local validity signals gate trajectory advantages so that intermediate recovery decisions do not indiscriminately inherit terminal outcomes. Across four repository-level software-engineering benchmarks, RIPPLE improves the base policy by an arithmetic mean of 4.8 score points, with no auxiliary critic at deployment. candidates.title: From Prompt Rules to Golden Data Model: Production-Scale Generation of Personalized, Compliant Pharmaceutical Claims
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.31519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate domain-specific commercial & medical content (e.g., claims, statements, and promotional phrases) in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals. However, ensuring its regulatory compliance, factual accuracy, and audience-specific personalization remains a major challenge. We report a production case study asking whether moving compliance and personalization signal from prompt-level rules into retrieval time structured context improves pharmaceutical claims generation, using Composer, a deployed internal tool built on a Golden Data Model (GDM) of 1,867 pharmaceutical claims spanning four products. The GDM integrates claim metadata, references, audience labels, material type, usage history, Match Text Variant (MTV) links, and a six dimension quality score (6C). Across six product-audience segments, the context pipeline improves intended indication (+29%), intended content type (+62%) and intended target audience (+67%), 6C quality score (+86%), and claim reuse (+34%).
